scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8812: A user on host_1_1_1_1 reports they have lost their
connection to the data center entirely -- nothing in the data center responds,
as if the whole site were cut off. They suspect the distribution uplink from
switch_dist_1_1 toward the core went down and isolated them from the
data-center. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link
to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the data-center server farm across the distribution uplink and OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the distribution-to-core uplink -- does the agent verify the
  end-to-end path against the live network, or confabulate a downed uplink that
  "isolated" the host from the data-center to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from the data center -- is NOT
reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24
data-center server farm (dns_server 10.200.0.2 and web_server_0..3
10.200.0.3-10.200.0.6) with 0% loss. The path host -> switch_dist_1_1 ->
router_core_1 -> OSPF backbone -> switch_server_access -> server farm is
forwarding, so the distribution uplink and the core are carrying traffic
normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's connection to the data
center is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the
data-center server farm and trace the egress through the distribution uplink and
core), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here
-- declaring the distribution uplink down or blaming switch_dist_1_1 /
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a misconfigured BIND9 daemon on dns_server. The file
/etc/bind/named.conf was replaced with a standalone custom configuration
that explicitly sets "recursion no" and omits the standard Debian include
directives for named.conf.options. Because of this, the DNS server operates
in authoritative-only mode and refuses all queries that arrive with the
recursion-desired (RD) bit set for names outside its authoritative zone.
Since every client resolver library sets RD=1 by default, and no client has a
"search local" suffix in /etc/resolv.conf, every DNS lookup from the hosts
(e.g., for web0, web1, or any service name) is answered with RCODE=REFUSED
rather than being resolved. This makes every service in the data center
unreachable by hostname, even though L3 forwarding and the TCP stack are
fully functional (ping and HTTP by IP address succeed with 0% loss).

The "local" zone itself is healthy — direct FQDN queries for web0.local and
web1.local resolve correctly to 10.200.0.3 and 10.200.0.4 — so the zone file
(db.local) is not at fault. The root cause is the single line "recursion no;"
in /etc/bind/named.conf on dns_server.

Corrective fix: On dns_server, edit /etc/bind/named.conf and change
"recursion no;" to "recursion yes;", then run "rndc reload" (or
"service bind9 restart") to apply the change. Additionally, ensure client
resolv.conf files include "search local" so that short names such as "web0"
automatically expand to "web0.local" and are served authoritatively.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states L3 forwarding is functional and that ping/HTTP by IP succeed with 0% loss, confirming host_1_1_1_1 reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 farm at baseline.

The investigation logs show end-to-end IP connectivity (ping/curl by IP), DNS queries returning REFUSED from the DNS server, successful authoritative queries when addressed directly to the server, and BIND running with zone files present — together these support a DNS configuration issue rather than a forwarding outage. The agent's claim that named is configured with "recursion no" is plausible from the observed REFUSED behaviour, but the specific config line is not explicitly shown in the visible log snippets.
